chunks: As for what was narrated — al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Sinan and 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, both together from Ibn Muskan, from Layth al-Muradi Abu Basir, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Utba al-Kufi al-Hashimi, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about a man who urinates and his right hand has not been touched by anything — should he insert it into his wudu water before washing it? He said: «No, not until he washes it.» I said: What if he has awoken from sleep without having urinated — may he insert his hand into his wudu water before washing it? He said: «No, because he does not know where his hand spent the night — so let him wash it.»

This report is interpreted as a recommendation (mustahabb) rather than an obligation (wajib), based on the evidence of the reports we have previously cited. He then said — may Allah the Exalted support him — that if [the water] constitutes a kurr, its measure being one thousand two hundred Iraqi ratls, it is not corrupted [by the insertion of an unwashed hand], even if it is stagnant.

key_terms.كُرّاً: kurr — minimum water volume (1,200 Iraqi ratls) resistant to ritual impurity
key_terms.وَضُوئِهِ: his wudu water — water prepared for ritual ablution

ai.seo_question: Must one wash the right hand before wudu after sleep according to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), and is this ruling obligatory or recommended?
ai.summary: This hadith records a ruling by Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) in response to 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Utba al-Hashimi: one must wash the right hand before immersing it in wudu water, both after urination and after waking from sleep, the latter because one cannot know where the hand rested during the night. Shaykh al-Tusi interprets the ruling as a recommendation (mustahabb) rather than an obligation (wajib) based on other narrations, and appends a ruling that kurr-quantity water (1,200 Iraqi ratls) is not rendered impure even if stagnant.
